pr_title: Fix setting and reading percentage for MIOT based fans
pr_body:

## Breaking change
<!--

  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
I'm not actually sure if this is considered a breaking change as it's current state is actually broken. 
However, if your automation relied on setting 1% to 4% to set the levels of the fan to the min, mid and max levels, then this will break it as 1% to 4% will now be mapped to level 1 (see below for behavior before and after). 


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Current behavior: 
setting 1, 2, 3 or 4 as percentage value strictly sets the level of miot fans (depending on model 3 or 4 is max). This means if you want to set the fan to the max power, you have to set it to 3% or 4% depending on your model. 
Additionally according to the code, the fan is supposed to turn on when you select a percentage. However, the fan needs to be turned on already to execute speed values (setting the value and then turning it on does not work as it seems). 

New behavior: 
All percentage values are mapped to the corresponding levels (the percentage is split into equal parts according to amount of levels the fan supports). Additionally the fan is turned on first if it was turned off and the speed is set immediately afterwards.

issue_context.title: Speed does not work for dmaker.fan.1c

Hey there @rytilahti, @syssi, @starkillerog, @bieniu, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`xiaomi_miio`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1231) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

---

[xiaomi_miio documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/xiaomi_miio)
[xiaomi_miio source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/xiaomi_miio)
<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

The issue seems to be that service "Fan: Set speed percentage" sends a percentage value (0 - 100) but dmaker.fan.1c only accepts values 1, 2 and 3 for its set_speed function.

Setting the fan speed works for now if using only values between 0 and 3 (0=off).

I second this, would be good to fix this. Either map percentage to 0, 1, 2, 3 or change the slider bar to only include options 1, 2, 3. 

I'm willing to support if anybody needs logs or anything to look into the issue. 

Update: 
I had a quick look into the other integration mentioned by op. 

They use presets with speed 0, 1, 2 ,3 and use  ordered_list_item_to_percentage and  percentage_to_ordered_list_item to map them to commands and read the current value back in percentage. So creating a new class for the 1c and overwriting in a specific class: 

```
self._percentage = self.coordinator.data.speed #using ordered list to percentage
```

and 
```
await self._try_command(
            "Setting fan speed percentage of the miio device failed.",
            self._device.set_speed,
            percentage, # use percentage_to_ordered_list here
        )
        self._percentage = percentage # that's not actually percentage I think and should reflect the speed preset
```
I created a PR open for review that fixes this and one other issue (fan does not turn on when you set percentage without turning fan on)

review_comments:
@MartinHjelmare I was thinking to set _percentage directly to the ranged value which would make it snap to the range borders instead of doing the same only when we get the state update in `_handle_coordinator_update directly` from the device. What do you think? 

Behavior before: 
 * set to percentage, e.g. 45%
 * will stay at 45% until we get the update of the device that speed 2 is now selected which will update percentage to something like 33% due to the ranged nature of mapping from speed to %

New behavior: 
 * set percentage, e.g. 45%
 * as soon as the command is executed the percentage snaps directly to the correctly ranged percentage, i.e. 33%.

The new behavior would omit the seemingly random jumps of the percentage due to the update from the device a few seconds after setting a new value.
